Figure 1. CRISP workflow for case-level histopathology representation from multi-slide whole-slide images: (A) Number of whole-slide images (WSIs) per case in the diagnostic study cohort. (B) Number of WSIs per diagnostic subtype, showing class imbalance across categories. (C) Number of whole-slide images (WSIs) per triple-negative breast cancer patient in the treatment study cohort. (D) Number of patients for positive and negative pathologic complete response (pCR). (E) Example patient (C02) with three WSIs used as case input. (F) Initial candidate patches sampled from tissue-rich regions of each WSI. (G) SPLICE-based pruning removes redundant or low-information patches (crossed tiles), retaining diverse, informative patches. (H) Aggregation of retained patches into a reduced case-level patch set across all WSIs from the same case. (I) Construction of Yottixel’s case mosaic via two-stage clustering and representative sampling. (J) Extraction of patch features using a vision foundation model (VFM). (K) Assembly of the final case embedding from patch-level features for downstream retrieval and classification.
